title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ reporting (cost optimization)
author: Jordan Kim
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching/caching, new quantization profile registry, and unit-economics tooling for cost reporting and recommendations.
description:
Motivation: Customers increasingly ask for automated knobs that reduce per-token cost without manual tuning. This change introduces a conservative autotune path that sets safe defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, wires in quantization profile selection, and surfaces unit-economics metrics in the Console and telemetry pipeline.

Summary of changes: 1) Autotune defaults: new heuristics to pick batch_size targets, request windowing, and conservative latency-safe cache retention policies. 2) Quant profiles: registry of recommended quantization profiles per model family + runtime selection logic and a compatibility matrix for fallbacks. 3) UEcon tooling: new telemetry events, aggregation transforms, and Console dashboard + CLI report for per-route unit cost and estimated savings if autotune/quant is applied. 4) Tests and docs: end-to-end integration tests for safety limits, performance regression checks, and updated docs/README.

Why this approach: We prioritize production safety—defaults never increase tail latency beyond configured SLOs and include gradual rollout via canary flags. Quant profiles are optional and require compatibility checks before being applied at runtime. UEcon tooling provides transparent cost impact so customers can opt into changes.

Checklist: - [x] Autotune heuristics implemented and unit-tested - [x] Quant profile registry and selection implemented - [x] Telemetry events and aggregation for unit-econ computed - [x] Console dashboard and CLI report added - [x] E2E tests (canary pipeline) - [x] Docs and API changelog updated - [x] Backwards compatibility tests

Migration notes: No mandatory migration. Customers can opt-in via the autotune=true flag or use the Console suggested profiles. For Dedicated/Private customers, quant profiles are disabled by default and require an admin toggle.

Risk and mitigation: The main risk is latent tail-latency regressions. Mitigations: conservative default thresholds, staged rollout, and automatic rollback if SLO breaches are detected.

Detailed implementation notes: - Autotune algorithm samples recent request size/latency histograms (last 5k requests) and proposes batch_size and max_queue_ms values; proposals are validated against a local latency simulator. - KV caching default retention depends on model sequence-length distribution; short-context workloads use longer retention windows. - Quant profile registry is a yaml-backed catalog in redwood-model-registry with semantic versioning; runtime picks the highest-ranked compatible profile, falls back to float32 if unsupported. - UEcon tooling adds per-request token counts, effective GPU-seconds, and estimated $ cost to telemetry; aggregation service computes 95th-mean unit cost per route and writes to metrics-store for Console graphs.

notes: This PR centralizes the cost-optimization defaults that previously lived in ad-hoc configs. Follow-ups planned: 1) automated rollback on SLO breach, 2) UI for one-click apply, 3) expanded quant profiles for more model families.
